chunks: "I shall go up a mountain," he said, "which will keep me from the water."
"There is no getting away," said Noah, "from the decree of God today, except for those on whom be His mercy."
And a wave came between them, and he was among those who were drowned.

key_terms.سَآوِي: I shall go up / seek refuge

ai.seo_question: What did Noah's son say he would do to escape the flood, and why was he ultimately drowned?
ai.summary: In this verse, Noah (AS) distinguishes between physical refuge and divine salvation, illustrating that worldly protections like mountains are insufficient against Allah's decree unless accompanied by mercy. Shia scholarship often highlights the contrast here between the son's reliance on material strength and the necessity of spiritual submission, a theme echoed in the concept of 'Amr Allah' (God's Command). The wave that separates them serves as a literal and metaphorical barrier, marking the son's exclusion from the saved community despite his blood relation to the Prophet.
